newsitem.title: INDIA: India awards top honours to Independence veterans.
newsitem.headline: India awards top honours to Independence veterans.

text.p: India on Thursday awarded its highest civilian honour to a 99-year-old independence leader who twice served as a stop-gap prime minister, and posthumously to a woman firebrand who died last year.
The presidential palace said in a communique: "The president is pleased to award the Bharat Ratna to Gulzari Lal Nanda and to the late Aruna Asaf Ali."
The awards were announced three weeks before the 50th anniversary of India's Independence on August 15.
The award went to Aruna Asaf Ali, a leftist veteran of India's movement for independence from British colonial rule, for her lifetime contribution to the country. She died in July 1996, aged 88.
Nanda, a staunch follower of Mahatma Gandhi, was given the award for his contribution to the national freedom movement and building up of the nation in its formative years.

Nanda twice served as country's interim prime minister. His first tenure as prime minister lasted only 15 days. He took over the administration after the death of Jawaharlal Nehru in 1964 before handing it over to Lal Bahadur Shastri.

In 1966, when Shastri died of a heart attack, Nanda again became interim prime minister. He handed over power to Indira Gandhi, daughter of India's first prime minister Jawaharlal Nehru, after 13 days.

Nanda was the first deputy chairman of independent India's Planning Commission and one of the brains behind the first five year-plan. He also served as Planning Minister in 1951/52 and Home Minister from 1963 to 1966.
He was jailed several times during India's struggle for independence.
Ali also went to jail between 1930 and 1947 -- the year in which India won independence. Eleven years later, she was elected Delhi's first mayor.
Ali, who was married to Asaf Ali, a leader of India's Congress party, in 1962 founded the Patriot, a left-leaning newspaper.
Moscow awarded her the Lenin Peace Prize in 1965.
